Accountability — watchlist vs just holding ETH or BTC

Equal weight, buy-and-hold; the 8/6 eight-to-seven seat change is carried in the series, never restated.

What you pay for $1 of net value flow — market cap ÷ (holders revenue − new supply)

The primary dial: market cap ÷ (holders revenue − new supply), both annualized. Lower = cheaper net cash flow. Names whose supply-in exceeds capture have no net multiple.

What you pay for $1 of holder revenue — market cap ÷ holders revenue (before dilution)

The secondary read: market cap ÷ holders revenue, before supply-in. Lower = more business per dollar.
Dashed = estimated basis. ETH and SOL hatched at the chart cap (off-scale). AAVE not charted — holders revenue prints zero; only its fee leg appears in History.

Value accrual & dilution notes

Curated by Claude — mechanisms and unlock overhangs the APIs don't carry. Verify dates before acting.
Discipline: separate hype/narrative from business fundamentals; a token qualifies only if its value appreciates in direct relationship to the business (fees, burns, buybacks, staking revenue). No memecoins. ETH in scope; BTC tracked separately.
Reading MC/FDV: low ratio = a large share of the eventual supply is still to come (deep dilution overhang); ~1.0 = fully diluted.
Data: live trackers first (CoinGecko, then Binance, then Hyperliquid); offline, the last verified snapshot is shown with its date. Fees are DefiLlama 30-day run-rates, annualized ×12.17; an unverifiable feed is carried at its last verified value.
Business grade (trial): a measured letter (A–E) from six checks on public revenue data, shown alongside the judged scores during a trial; it does not yet drive rankings.
Legend: T1 = on-chain / independently verified · T2 = project-official · T3 = named analyst/press · est = estimate · net-dilutive = new supply currently exceeds the value paid to holders.
